answer: Price elapsed time, not stake. At random a verifier sends each identity a nonce; it must return a hash chain whose steps depend on the last, within a tight window. Such work cannot be split across cores or precomputed, so a farmer running a thousand aliases on one box must queue them, and that queue leaks. Replies arrive in a shared, staggered pulse; lockstep timing clusters accounts as one host, whose weight falls to the nadir of a single member. Honest machines jitter independently, like grain in timber. Keys cannot buy clocks, so cloning reveals itself through correlation.
